<!-- Generated by `chainmail docs`. Do not edit: change the command's help and run `go tool stave docs:commands`. -->

Search mail with Gmail-style operators. Terms are joined by AND, -term
negates, OR joins (it binds tighter than AND, as in Gmail), parentheses
group, and values with spaces are quoted.

```text
word, "a phrase"              text anywhere in the message
from: to: cc: bcc:            address or display name contains
subject:                      subject contains
is:unread is:read is:starred
newer_than: older_than:       days, weeks, months or years: 7d, 2w, 3m, 1y
after: before:                YYYY-MM-DD
larger: smaller:              bytes, or KiB and MiB: 10K, 5M
has:attachment filename: label:
                              Google accounts, and other accounts once
                              their cache is complete (see chainmail
                              cache status); label: there matches IMAP
                              keywords
in:                           inbox, sent, drafts, archive, trash, spam
                              (or junk), anywhere, or a folder name
account:                      this account; each account: term and each
                              --account adds one
item:                         mail in threads linked to this item or any
                              item below it; item:none, mail in threads
                              linked to no item. Only the cache answers
                              these, never the mail server
```

Every folder except Trash and Spam is searched unless in: says otherwise.
On accounts other than Google, dates work at day granularity on the arrival
date, so newer\_than:1d there matches since the start of yesterday.

Each account is answered from the local cache when the cache can answer
the whole query and is fresh, and by its mail server otherwise. The table
output ends with a source line naming which answered each account.
\--source cache answers from the cache even when it is incomplete or stale,
and says why; --source server skips the cache.

The shell removes quotes, so quote the whole query when it holds a phrase
or a quoted value, as in the second example below. Put -- before the query
when a term starts with -, so it is not read as a flag:

```text
chainmail search -- invoice -from:acme
```

## Usage

```text
chainmail search [query...] [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
chainmail search invoice from:acme newer_than:30d
chainmail search 'subject:"q3 report" OR has:attachment' --account gmail
chainmail search is:unread in:inbox --count
chainmail search from:acme --source server
```

## Flags

```text
      --account stringArray   only this account (repeatable)
      --count                 count matches instead of listing them
      --cursor string         continue from the previous page's cursor
      --limit uint32          rows per page, at most 500 (default 50)
      --snippet               add a snippet of up to 200 characters to each row
      --source string         where answers come from: auto, cache or server (default auto: the cache when it is complete and fresh)
      --threads               show the newest message of each thread
```

## Global flags

```text
      --output string   output format: json or table (default $CHAINMAIL_OUTPUT, then cli.toml, then table on a terminal, json otherwise)
      --socket string   daemon socket (default $CHAINMAIL_SOCKET, then cli.toml, then /run/chainmail/chainmail.sock)
```
